scenes.vo: Part two. It's seven nine. There's a grey sleeve outside my door, and a library book that knows my morning.
scenes.cap: Part 2. 7:09. A grey sleeve at my door. A book that knows my morning.

scenes.vo: I didn't open the door. I sat on the floor and turned to the last page again.
scenes.cap: I didn't open the door. I turned to the last page again.

scenes.vo: The words had changed. It now said: she did not open the door, so he left something for her.
scenes.cap: The page had changed: "She did not open the door. So he left something for her."

scenes.vo: At seven ten, the knocking stopped. Footsteps went down the stairs. Then nothing.
scenes.cap: 7:10. The knocking stopped. Footsteps. Then nothing.

scenes.vo: On my doormat was an envelope. Inside, a handwritten note. I wrote this book forty years ago. Nobody ever finished it. You did.
scenes.cap: On the mat, a note: "I wrote this book 40 years ago. Nobody finished it. You did."

scenes.vo: The last line said: please, write the ending. Under it, the pages were blank.
scenes.cap: "Please write the ending." The rest of the pages: blank.

scenes.vo: So I'm writing it now. About a woman at midnight, reading a library book. Tomorrow, it might be on your desk.
scenes.cap: So I'm writing it now. Tomorrow, it might be on YOUR desk.
